# Sirach Chapter 41 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 41 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 41 divides into two distinct parts: (1) a meditation on death (vv. 1–13) and (2) a catalog of things of which to be ashamed (vv. 14–27). The opening address to death as both bitter and welcome is one of Sirach's most rhetorically elegant moments. The shame catalog in vv. 16–27 presents translation challenges around social hierarchy terms.

**Key term decisions:**
- "sentence / decree" for the divine judgment of death (krisison): LOGOS "sentence," EMET "decree" — SOPHIA adopts "decree" as more solemn
- v. 11: "evil name" (onoma ponēron) vs. "bad name" vs. "foul name" — SOPHIA adopts "evil name" as most literal
- v. 14: "in peace" (en eirēnē) — all agents agree this is an adverbial phrase modifying how one should hold to instruction
- v. 22: "prostitute" (pornē) — all agents agree; no euphemism warranted
- v. 20: "leaning on your elbow" — idiomatic for reclining at table in Hellenistic dining custom

---

**41:1** O death, how bitter is the memory of you to someone at peace in his possessions — a man with no distractions, prosperous in all things, and still strong enough to enjoy food!

**41:2** O death, how welcome is your decree to one who is in need and whose strength fails, who is worn down with age and overwhelmed by every care, to one who has lost all patience and abandoned hope!

**41:3** Do not fear the decree of death. Remember those who came before you and those who will come after. This is the Lord's decree upon all flesh.

**41:4** And why do you resist the good pleasure of the Most High? Whether ten years or a hundred or a thousand — there is no reckoning about the length of life in Hades.

**41:5** The children of sinners are abominable children, and they frequent the haunts of the ungodly.

**41:6** The inheritance of sinners' children will be destroyed, and perpetual reproach will cling to their descendants.

**41:7** Children curse an ungodly father, for they bear reproach on his account.

**41:8** Woe to you, O ungodly men, who have forsaken the law of the Most High God!

**41:9** When you are born, you are born into a curse; and when you die, a curse is your portion.

**41:10** All that comes from the earth returns to the earth; so the ungodly go from curse to destruction.

**41:11** The mourning of men is over their bodies, but the evil name of sinners will be blotted out.

**41:12** Have regard for your name, for it will outlast you longer than a thousand great treasuries of gold.

**41:13** The days of a good life are few, but a good name endures forever.

**41:14** My children, keep instruction in peace — hidden wisdom and unseen treasure, what is the profit in either?

**41:15** Better is the person who conceals his folly than one who conceals his wisdom.

**41:16** Therefore show proper shame in these things I am about to speak of, for it is not good to show partiality in every matter:

**41:17** Be ashamed before father and mother of sexual immorality, and before a ruler or a powerful person of a lie;

**41:18** before a master and a mistress of wrongdoing; before a congregation and a people of a lawless act;

**41:19** before a companion and a friend of injustice; and in the place where you dwell, of theft.

**41:20** Be ashamed of the truth of God and his covenant, and of reclining on your elbow at table;

**41:21** of selfishness in giving and receiving, and of silence toward those who greet you;

**41:22** of gazing at a prostitute, and of turning away your face from a kinsman;

**41:23** of taking away someone's portion and not returning it, and of fixing your eye on another man's wife;

**41:24** of meddling with his servant girl — do not approach her bed;

**41:25** of reproachful words before friends, and of taunting someone after giving to them;

**41:26** of repeating what you have heard and of disclosing secrets.

**41:27** Then you will be truly modest, and you will find favor with every person.
